subject.title: Chronic agent failures on Telegram — LLM timeouts before configured timeout + silent incomplete turns + dead fallbacks (OpenRouter/DeepSeek+V4-Flash, v2026.5.28)

question: Should this composite Telegram/OpenRouter reliability issue stay open pending a maintainer-led current-release repro with effective config and runId-level logs, or is the existing component-fix evidence enough to close it?
rationale: Current source fixes several linked component paths, but the report combines provider timeout configuration, fallback decisions, and Telegram block-stream delivery, and the available diagnostics are from an older release without effective config attached.

options.title: Keep for current-run correlation
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for or run a v2026.6.11/current-main Telegram/OpenRouter trace with sanitized models.providers.openrouter.timeoutSeconds, fallback config, and runId logs.

options.title: Close as component-fixed
options.body: Close only if a maintainer accepts that provider timeout wiring, timeout fallback tests, and block-stream error preservation cover the observed user problem without fresh reproduction.

options.title: Split into narrower follow-ups
options.body: Close this cluster only after creating or linking narrower canonical issues for any remaining timeout-config, fallback, or Telegram delivery behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep for current-run correlation
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and ask for or run a v2026.6.11/current-main Telegram/OpenRouter trace with sanitized models.providers.openrouter.timeoutSeconds, fallback config, and runId logs.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to the earlier timeout/fallback closure and timeout-policy history, making him the best available owner for the proof-sufficiency call across this composite cluster.
